description: CDSI (contact discovery) vectors for spec/service/cdsi.md. All hex is lowercase. Numbers are 8-byte big-endian unsigned integers; ACI/PNI are 16 raw UUID bytes; ClientRequest/ClientResponse are protobuf (package org.signal.cdsi, field tables in cdsi.md section 4).
source: libsignal v0.99.1 (97801d22dcf9f5bf714f7b8fa3212cdc973ae1c8) rust/net/src/cdsi.rs unit tests (published vectors, marked 'published'); rust/attest/src/constants.rs and rust/net/src/enclave.rs (enclave id, path); ContactDiscoveryService-Icelake tag 1.25.2 (46540d24ca3437f0100fd53ba2024192d69115f5) for server behaviour; access keys computed offline with the signal-cli 0.14.7 bundled libsignal-client 0.99.1 jar (ProfileKey.deriveAccessKey); protobuf messages constructed by hand from the field layout (marked 'constructed') and cross-checked with protoc --decode_raw.

staging_endpoint.auth_endpoint: GET /v2/directory/auth (authenticated chat websocket), response {"username":string,"password":string}, used as HTTP Basic on the enclave websocket upgrade

aci_access_key_serialization.provenance: published (libsignal cdsi.rs test serialize_acis_and_access_keys): for i in 1..5, ACI = 16 bytes of (i|0x80), access key = 16 bytes of i

response_parse_published.provenance: published (libsignal cdsi.rs test parse_lookup_response_entries): the same 40-byte triple repeated 4 times, debug_permits_used 42, token empty
response_parse_published.note: libsignal yields 4 identical records; as a map keyed by number (what signal-cli uses) this is one entry.

access_keys.provenance: derived offline with the reference jar (ProfileKey.deriveAccessKey); algorithm in spec/service/api.md section 5.1

fixed_width_service_ids.provenance: derived offline with the reference jar (toServiceIdFixedWidthBinary); the CDSI pair uses the UUID bytes only, without the type byte

client_request_full.provenance: constructed from the field layout (cdsi.md 4.1); access key derived with the jar; token bytes are arbitrary (version byte 1, then 0x20..0x5f) and not a server-valid token
client_request_full.note: Fields appear in number order 1,2,3,6; empty discard_e164s (4) and false token_ack (7) are omitted. Entry order inside the e164 and pair fields is not significant (signal-cli iterates hash sets).

client_request_partial.provenance: constructed from the field layout; a partial lookup as signal-cli sends it, but with no aci_uak_pairs (account with no known profile keys)

client_token_ack.provenance: constructed from the field layout (ClientRequest with only token_ack=true)

server_token_response.provenance: constructed from the field layout (ClientResponse with only token)

server_final_response.provenance: constructed from the field layout and the Icelake masking rule (not-found number => all-zero 40-byte record, ACI zero when no matching ACI/UAK pair)
server_final_response.note: The third record (all zeros) is the server's answer for +18005551002 and must be skipped; that number is then treated as not found.

response_errors.provenance: derived from libsignal cdsi.rs parsing rule
response_errors.expected: protocol error: could not parse response triples (41 bytes)

response_errors.case: first server message has empty token
response_errors.expected: protocol error: no token found in response

close_codes.provenance: published (libsignal cdsi.rs CdsiCloseCode and tests websocket_close_with_rate_limit_exceeded_*, websocket_invalid_token_close); server side: Icelake WebSocketHandler

cases.expected: invalid token (signal-cli clears cdsi-token and the cdsi table)
invalid argument (signal-cli clears cdsi-token and the cdsi table)

e164_string_parsing.provenance: derived from libsignal rust/core/src/e164.rs (strip one leading '+', then Rust NonZeroU64 decimal parse, which itself accepts one leading '+')
e164_string_parsing.note: Any rejected string fails the whole lookup before connecting (IllegalArgumentException -> treated as CDSI invalid argument by signal-cli).
